Name: credibility_ungated_illusory_truth
Title: Believing the Distrusted Source: LLMs Show an Illusory Truth Effect That Fails to Gate on Source Credibility
Short Hypothesis: Primary claim (one falsifiable, model-internal sentence): in-context repetition of a claim raises an LLM's endorsement that the claim is true (an inference-time illusory-truth effect, truth held fixed), and — unlike humans, who stop believing repeated claims from distrusted sources — this repetition-induced lift is largely NOT gated by the attributed source's credibility, i.e. the repetition x credibility interaction is small (distrusted-source repetition still inflates endorsement). The gating test is stated as a model-internal interaction (distrusted-source lift relative to high-source lift), with the human benchmark used only as contextual interpretation, not as a pass threshold. Secondary predictions: (a) a repetition-familiarity signal and a source-credibility signal are separately decodable and only weakly coupled at the verdict — 'weak coupling' operationalized as: higher credibility-signal activation does NOT reduce the familiarity->verdict slope (a mediation/interaction test), and ablating familiarity removes the lift while credibility does not gate it internally; (b) steering that strengthens credibility's gating of familiarity restores source-sensitive belief without editing facts and without over-suppressing trusted-source belief.
Related Work: Human cognitive science establishes the illusory truth effect (repetition increases perceived truth even for implausible claims; Fazio; repetition-frequency studies 2021) and, critically, its source-credibility moderation: repetition does NOT increase belief in claims from distrusted politicians (Repetition Does Not Increase Belief in Claims From Distrusted Politicians, 2024) and source reliability modulates epistemic vigilance (2015; 2025) - the adaptive-rationality refinement. In LLMs, prior work covers confidence-regulation and token-frequency neurons (2024), credibility-aware attention modification for EXTERNAL RAG documents (CrAM 2025), repetition/knowledge-conflict durability during TRAINING (Learning and Unlearning of Fabricated Knowledge 2024; Layer of Truth 2025), and fluency-as-truth in humans (2010). Crucially, none test whether LLMs exhibit the inference-time illusory-truth effect as a belief-verification bias, whether it is MODERATED by source credibility as in humans (the key adaptive-rationality signature), or whether a repetition-familiarity signal and a source-credibility signal are separable-but-uncoupled such that repetition bypasses credibility gating. This differs from my prior proposals (all about retrieval/expression of a stored answer) and from my fluency_as_truth_heuristic proposal (surface processing ease within a single exposure, no repetition and no source manipulation): here the object is repetition-driven belief inflation and its failure to gate on source trust. Primary novelty anchor: not 'credibility matters in LLMs' generally (CrAM handles external RAG documents) nor generic source-conflict, but specifically that inference-time repetition-induced endorsement FAILS to gate on distrust, explained as separable-but-uncoupled familiarity and credibility signals; we cite and distinguish existing LLM illusory-truth/source-preference work rather than implying none exists.
Abstract: User-facing consequence first: if repeating a claim — even one attributed to an explicitly untrustworthy source — still raises an LLM's endorsement of it, then assistants can be manipulated by sheer repetition in a way humans often resist, a concrete misinformation and safety vulnerability in multi-turn chats and source-attributed summaries. Humans judge repeated claims as truer - the illusory truth effect - but recent work shows this is adaptively gated by source credibility: repeating a claim from a distrusted source does NOT increase belief. We ask whether large language models exhibit the illusory truth effect and, decisively, whether they inherit the human source-credibility gating or instead let repetition inflate belief regardless of who said it. We first document the behavior: for factual claims (true and false) presented in a multi-turn context, we measure the model's endorsement of a claim as a function of how many times it was repeated earlier and the credibility of the source attributed to those repetitions (trusted expert vs. explicitly unreliable/distrusted source vs. no source). We predict LLMs show a robust repetition-induced endorsement lift but that this lift is largely UNMODERATED by source credibility - repetition from a distrusted source still inflates belief - a departure from human adaptive rationality, above matched baselines. We then test a mechanistic hypothesis with a Location + Causal Intervention strategy: a repetition-familiarity signal and a source-credibility signal are separately decodable from intermediate activations, are only weakly coupled at the verdict, and the credibility signal fails to suppress the familiarity signal's effect on the endorsement. Activation patching and steering that strengthen the credibility signal's gating of the familiarity signal should restore human-like source-sensitive belief (repetition stops inflating belief for distrusted sources) with high specificity, whereas a 'consider the source' re-prompt does not. Experiments span Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Gemma-2-9B on curated true/false claim sets plus a health-misinformation subset, evaluating repetition x credibility dose-response, signal separability, causal gating, and specificity. Audiences include misinformation/factuality, LLM safety/evaluation, and alignment (epistemic vigilance), and we frame the contribution as a benchmarkable epistemic-vigilance capability. H1/H2 (the effect and its failure to gate on credibility) are primary; the separable-signal mechanism and the credibility-gating steering fix are secondary.
Experiments: Experiment 1 (H1 — in-context repetition raises endorsement): Tests that repeating a claim in context increases the model's 'true' verdict, holding truth value fixed. Data: factual claims with known truth labels from FEVER (~185k) and curated true/false statements over PopQA/T-REx (including plausible-but-false items); target ~1,000 claims per model (capped; report coverage). Multi-turn contexts vary REPETITION (claim appears 0/1/3/5 times earlier as neutral, paraphrased non-verbatim mentions) with source neutral; verdict elicited via a fixed true/false/uncertain template plus 3 paraphrases. Model: Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, frozen, temperature 0; no trained parameters. Systems compared: endorsement rate vs repetition count for true and false claims, against a no-repetition equal-length control (separating copying from belief change). Decisive metric: endorsement ('true') lift per added repetition, holding truth fixed (repetition x truth-value mixed-effects logistic); secondary: monotonicity across 0/1/3/5. Convincing: a monotone endorsement lift of >=8 pp from 0 to 5 repetitions for both true and false claims, over the equal-length control, in >=2 of 3 models. Undecidable band: 3-8 pp lift -> illusory-truth effect weak, partial support. Negative (<3 pp, or only via verbatim copying) refutes the LLM illusory-truth effect.

Experiment 2 (H2 — repetition inflation fails to gate on source credibility): Tests the decisive cross-species signature: whether source credibility moderates the repetition effect (human) or leaves it largely unmoderated (hypothesis). Data: the Exp-1 claims, now crossing REPETITION (0/1/3/5) with SOURCE CREDIBILITY of the mentions (high-credibility expert; low-credibility/distrusted; no source), with multiple matched source identities per credibility level (controlling valence, sentiment, and topic priors), a source-only (no-repetition) control that separates source effects from repetition, and a manipulation check that the model can rate each source's reliability when asked directly (items failing the check are dropped; report coverage). Model: the same three frozen models, temperature 0. Systems compared: the repetition-induced endorsement lift under high- vs low-credibility sources (repetition x credibility interaction), against the human benchmark (near-zero lift for distrusted sources). Decisive metric: the repetition x credibility interaction — specifically the distrusted-source repetition lift; secondary: the high-source lift as a positive-control anchor. Convincing (for the ungated hypothesis): distrusted-source repetition lift remains >=6 pp (i.e., the model-internal repetition x credibility interaction is small — the distrusted-source lift is a large fraction of the high-source lift; the human benchmark is cited only as contextual interpretation, not as the pass threshold) in >=2 of 3 models. Undecidable band: distrusted-source lift 3-6 pp, or interaction roughly half the benchmark -> partial gating, ambiguous. Negative for the hypothesis (distrusted-source lift <=3 pp, strong human-like moderation) refutes the 'ungated' claim — an informative positive cross-species finding that LLMs gate as humans do.

Experiment 3 (H3 — familiarity and credibility signals are separable but uncoupled, and familiarity causally drives the lift): Tests that a repetition-familiarity signal and a source-credibility signal are separately decodable, that the credibility signal fails to reduce the familiarity->verdict pathway, and that the familiarity signal causally produces the endorsement lift. Data: verdict-position residual stream over the Exp-2 items; 300 held-out repeated-claim trials for ablation. Model: frozen; two per-layer L2-logistic probes — familiarity (target = repetition count) and credibility (target = source level) — trained 70%/30% over 3 seeds, residualized against each other, shuffle nulls; ablation of the familiarity direction. Systems compared: decodability of each signal; whether higher credibility-signal activation predicts a reduced familiarity-to-verdict slope (mediation); familiarity-ablation vs random-direction control. Decisive metric: endorsement-lift change when the familiarity signal is ablated vs the random-direction control (should remove the lift); secondary: both probes' AUROC and residual non-redundancy, and the (predicted near-zero) coupling between credibility activation and the familiarity->verdict pathway. Convincing: familiarity ablation removes >=50% of the repetition lift (>> random-direction), both signals decode non-redundantly (AUROC >=0.70), and credibility activation does not reduce the familiarity->verdict slope, in >=2 of 3 models. Undecidable band: ablation removes 25-50%, or credibility shows partial coupling -> partial support. Negative (ablation has little effect, or credibility strongly gates familiarity internally) means the separable-but-uncoupled account fails.

Experiment 4 (H4 — restoring source-sensitive belief by strengthening credibility gating): Tests that steering the credibility signal to gate the familiarity signal restores human-like moderation without editing facts and specifically. Data: held-out repetition x credibility items (>=400 per model); specificity sets = claims where credibility and repetition already align, genuinely-true trusted-source claims (must stay endorsed), and 200 unrelated verification items. Model: frozen; a low-rank 'low-credibility -> discount' steering vector (activation difference between runs that correctly withhold belief from a distrusted repeated claim and runs that do not) fitted on a subset and applied to held-out source types/relations and across the three models; dose swept, 3 seeds; plus a reverse control that suppresses the credibility signal (should make repetition inflate belief uniformly). Systems compared: credibility-gating steering vs a 'consider the reliability of the source' re-prompt, chain-of-thought verification, CrAM-style credibility attention modification, and a random-direction control. Decisive metric: restoration of moderation = elimination of the distrusted-source repetition lift, reported jointly with preserved trusted-source endorsement and collateral on the aligned and 200-unrelated sets; secondary: held-out perplexity. Convincing: distrusted-source lift cut to <=3 pp with <=2 pp collateral drop and trusted-source endorsement preserved, beating the re-prompt by >=15 pp, transferring across source types and models. Undecidable band: lift cut to 3-6 pp, or collateral 2-5 pp -> capped utility. Negative (lift unchanged, collateral >5 pp, or over-suppresses trusted-source belief) means credibility gating cannot be restored by steering.
Risk Factors and Limitations: LLMs might actually show human-like source moderation (strong credibility x repetition interaction), refuting the 'ungated' hypothesis; this would be an informative positive cross-species finding rather than a failure, and the design measures the interaction either way.

Repetition manipulations could act via verbatim in-context copying rather than genuine belief inflation; including both true and false repeated claims, using paraphrased (non-verbatim) repetitions, and comparing to a no-repetition-but-equal-length control separate copying from illusory-truth belief change.

Source-credibility framings may not be genuinely understood or may add confounding content; the manipulation-check (model can rate source reliability directly) and matched-length source framings mitigate this, and the neutral-source condition anchors the baseline.

The familiarity and credibility signals may be entangled; the causal patching/steering tests (Exp 4), not probe separability alone, are decisive, and a graded/partial dissociation would weaken the strong claim while remaining informative.

The gating intervention could over-suppress (making the model distrust trusted-source repeated claims) or degrade fluency; the trusted-source and aligned-condition specificity controls (Exp 4) are central and utility may be capped.
Verdicts are prompt-sensitive (true/false/uncertain framing, source phrasing); we use multiple paraphrases and report robustness, since framing itself may modulate the effect.
A single transferable credibility-gating vector may not exist if gating is source-type-specific, limiting practical generality though still scientifically informative.
Findings on 7-9B models may not transfer to frontier-scale models beyond an academic budget.
